obligations.summary: The Commission, market surveillance authorities, notified bodies, and any other natural or legal person involved in applying this Regulation must respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks, protecting intellectual property rights, trade secrets, public security interests, criminal/administrative proceedings, and classified information.
exceptions: Confidentiality of intellectual property and trade secrets does not apply in cases referred to in Article 5 of Directive (EU) 2016/943.

obligations.summary: Authorities involved in applying this Regulation must request only data strictly necessary for risk assessment, implement adequate cybersecurity measures to protect obtained information, and delete collected data as soon as it is no longer needed for the purpose for which it was obtained.

Confidential information exchanged between national competent authorities or between those authorities and the Commission must not be disclosed without prior consultation of the originating national competent authority and the deployer when high-risk AI systems used by law enforcement, border control, immigration, or asylum authorities are involved and disclosure would jeopardise public or national security interests.
exceptions: Sensitive operational data relating to the activities of law enforcement, border control, immigration, or asylum authorities is excluded from such information exchange.

Paragraphs 1, 2, and 3 do not affect rights or obligations regarding exchange of information, dissemination of warnings, cross-border cooperation, or obligations to provide information under criminal law of Member States.

obligations.summary: When law enforcement, immigration, or asylum authorities act as providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III points 1, 6, or 7, technical documentation per Annex IV must remain within those authorities' premises, and those authorities must ensure that market surveillance authorities can, upon request, immediately access or obtain a copy of such documentation, restricted to staff with appropriate security clearance.
exceptions: Only staff of the market surveillance authority holding the appropriate level of security clearance may access the documentation or any copy thereof.

obligations.summary: The Commission and Member States may exchange confidential information with regulatory authorities of third countries where necessary and in accordance with relevant international and trade agreements, provided bilateral or multilateral confidentiality arrangements guaranteeing an adequate level of confidentiality are in place.
